newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to begin new wheat auctions November 18.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to begin new wheat auctions November 18.

text.p: The Brazilian government is to hold its first two auctions of domestic wheat on November 18 and November 22 in a new system which will guarantee the minimum price, said an official at Banco do Brasil.
The auctions, both of which are for up to 100,000 tonnes, will set not an outright price but the level of the subsidy to be paid by the government.
The buyer then pays the government the minimum price of 157 reais ($152.43) minus the subsidy set in the auction while the government pays the farmer the full 157 reais.
The sales which are to start at 1230 local/1430 GMT will consist of twelve lots, the Banco do Brasil official said.
The first four lots, each of 10,000 tonnes, will be of wheat from Rio Grande do Sul state.

The first will be for delivery in the north/northeast of the country, the second in Rio de Janeiro or Espirito Santo states, the third for delivery in Minas Gerais and Goias and the last for Sao Paulo state, he added.
The next four lots, each of 5,000 tonnes from Santa Catarina and the third set of four lots of 10,000 tonnes of wheat from Parana will follow the same pattern, he added.
Millers anticipate almost all of Brazil's 1996 harvest, estimated at 2.8 million to 3.2 million tonnes, will be sold in this way.
Without the system, domestic producers had feared millers would import Argentine wheat which currently is being quoted at $144 a tonne.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
